doc.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024

title: Larry as critic, and her record collecting youth with brother Peter
summary: Bunnett and Larry critique each other's music; Larry's early jazz concert-going contrasts with her eclectic record listening and brother Peter's collection.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Do you and Larry comment on each other’s music and composing and so forth.

Yes we sure do. He’s my worst critic and I’m his worst critic. Larry’s — but you know what it’s really, really great because yeah — his taste — he started working at a record store when he was like 15 years old and he’s attended way more jazz performances than I have because he was like in his late teens he was already going out and driving to Buffalo with people to hear — to hear Freddie Hubbard or to hear some of the greats that were playing. And I was still kind of back listening to, you know, my Joni Mitchell records and Bob Dylan before I got deeper into jazz. You know I came at it from a very eclectic record collection because I kind of liked all kinds of music when I was young. And my big brother Peter Bunnett, he was a pretty strong jazz fan and into beat poetry and he had everything. And I used to just love going into his room and pulling records out and putting them on and seeing what else was out there. So — but what I’m trying to say is like Larry is very — I think he’s got very great taste and big ears and has heard a lot of music.
